acceptance_criteria.criterion: renderNotesCollected() fetches display settings via api.config.notesDisplay.get() in parallel with api.notes.list() using Promise.all
Display settings fetch uses .catch(() => ({})) for graceful degradation
When notesColumns is present, grid-template-columns is set as inline style on .notes-main to repeat(N, 1fr)
When notesCardHeight is present, --notes-card-height CSS custom property is set on .notes-main container
.notes-card CSS rule in styles.css uses height: var(--notes-card-height, 220px) instead of fixed 220px
Notes view renders correctly with CSS defaults when display settings fetch fails

summary: Integrated notes display settings into the Notes Collected view with graceful degradation. Two changes made: (1) renderNotesCollected() now fetches api.config.notesDisplay.get() in parallel with api.notes.list() via Promise.all, with .catch(() => ({})) ensuring the view always renders even if the settings endpoint fails; (2) When notesColumns is present in the response, grid-template-columns is set as an inline style on .notes-main; when notesCardHeight is present, --notes-card-height CSS custom property is set on .notes-main. CSS updated: .notes-card height changed from fixed 220px to var(--notes-card-height, 220px) so the card height is controlled by the custom property with 220px fallback. All 834 server-side tests pass.

comments.note: notes-collected.js: The `displaySettings` variable could benefit from a JSDoc type annotation (e.g., `/** @type {{ notesColumns?: number, notesCardHeight?: number }} */`) to make the shape explicit for future readers, since the catch fallback of `{}` means TypeScript/editors can only infer `object`.

notes-collected.js: The `notesCardHeight` value is coerced to a pixel string via template literal (`${displaySettings.notesCardHeight}px`). If the API ever returns a value already including units, this would double them. The current API spec (notesCardHeight is always an integer) makes this safe, but a comment or guard could make the contract explicit.

gui/public/css/styles.css: The --notes-card-height CSS custom property is only defined on .notes-main when the API returns a value. Cascade is intentional here — CSS var() fallback handles the absence. This is correct, but a code comment on the CSS rule would help future maintainers understand why there is no explicit custom property declaration at :root.

comments.note: notesColumns=0 and notesCardHeight=0: Both if-guards use truthiness, so 0 values are skipped (no style applied). 0 columns is semantically invalid CSS so skipping is correct behaviour. Low risk.

Promise.all catch placement: .catch(() => ({})) is scoped only to the settings fetch — api.notes.list() rejections still surface to the outer try/catch and display the error toast as expected. Error isolation is correct.

notesCardHeight unit assumption: `${displaySettings.notesCardHeight}px` appends 'px' unconditionally. Safe per current API spec (integer only), but would produce malformed CSS (e.g. '300pxpx') if the API ever returns a string with units. A defensive guard or comment would future-proof this.

summary: [PASS] Code review complete. Implementation is clean, well-structured, and architecturally sound. Promise.all with scoped .catch isolates the non-critical settings fetch correctly. comments.note: notes-collected.js line 262: Added `/** @type {{ notesColumns?: number, notesCardHeight?: number }} */` JSDoc annotation to the `displaySettings` variable. The `.catch(() => ({}))` fallback arm causes editors/TypeScript to infer `object` rather than the actual shape — the annotation makes the contract explicit without changing any runtime behaviour.

[documentation-forward] notes-collected.js lines 303–304: The `${displaySettings.notesCardHeight}px` template literal appends 'px' unconditionally. Add an inline comment referencing the `NotesDisplayConfig` typedef (api.js line 107) which documents `notesCardHeight` as `{number}` (integer pixels, range 120–800) — this makes the unit assumption explicit and guides future readers who might wonder whether the `px` suffix is always safe.

[documentation-forward] styles.css .notes-card rule (line 1757): `height: var(--notes-card-height, 220px)` uses a CSS custom property that has no `:root` declaration — it is set dynamically by JS only when the API returns a value. A brief comment on this rule (e.g., `/* --notes-card-height set dynamically by renderNotesCollected(); 220px is the CSS fallback */`) would prevent future maintainers from wondering whether the missing `:root` declaration is an oversight.

No blocking or high-priority issues found. Architecture of the Promise.all with scoped .catch is the correct pattern for this use case — notes list failure must surface as an error, while display settings failure must degrade gracefully. Error isolation is correct and intentional.
